subject: Quick follow-up: private VPC eligibility & network questions
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@acmecorp.com>, Tariq Ahmed <tariq@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up: private VPC eligibility & network questions
Attachments: redwood-vpc-quickstart.pdf

Hi Lena / Tariq — thanks again for your time on the call today. Quick recap and the handful of items we need to qualify to confirm a Private VPC deployment (vs Dedicated or Hosted):

Summary of what we heard:
- You prefer a Private VPC deployment because of in-VPC traffic controls and auditability.
- Primary workloads: inference for customer-facing product (low-latency), plus internal batch embeddings runs.
- Compliance note: all inference traffic must not traverse public internet egress from your VPC.

Questions / items we need from your side to proceed:
1) Preferred connectivity model: do you require AWS PrivateLink (no peering allowed) or will VPC peering / Transit Gateway be acceptable?
2) Do you need a static set of outbound IPs (egress) for allowlisting, or is NAT + ephemeral IPs acceptable?
3) Are you planning to use a shared VPC (Transit GW) or an account-per-environment model? Please share the AWS account IDs and VPC IDs for the target subnets if possible.
4) Which subnets can we use for ENIs (public/private)? Do you enforce stricter security groups (lockdown per-port) or rely on NACLs?
5) KMS/HSM requirement: will keys be customer-managed and must reside in your KMS?
6) Certificate/TLS expectations for mutual TLS (mTLS) or simple TLS?

Next steps I propose:
- Please send a short network diagram (VPC/subnet, NAT/GW, transit) and the contact for your infra/network engineer.
- We'll schedule a 30-min technical sync between your infra team and our network engineer (Karthik) to verify routing and egress options.
- I attached our VPC quickstart doc that outlines both PrivateLink and peering options and required artifacts.

If you prefer we can also provision a short, time-boxed Dedicated pool as a fallback while we finish networking for VPC — happy to discuss trade-offs.

Can you share the network diagram and availability for a technical call next week?

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
(dylan@redwood.ai)

Hi Dylan — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a Private VPC deployment is our preference for the reasons stated on the call. A few quick answers and clarifications:

1) PrivateLink preferred: our security policy currently disallows peering across accounts for vendor connections. We generally use PrivateLink for managed services.
2) Static egress IPs are required for some of our external vendor allowlists (we can provide the list of destinations if that helps).
3) We're operating multiple accounts but would like to use a single shared service VPC (Transit Gateway) pattern for vendor connectivity.
4) We will share a network diagram and the account/VPC IDs — looped in is Tariq (infra) who will coordinate.
5) KMS: customer-managed keys required.
6) TLS: standard TLS is fine, mTLS is preferable for elevated endpoints.

We have a hard compliance checkpoint in 3 weeks; if we can validate the connectivity model and egress behavior within that window, we can proceed to procurement. Willing to take a short Dedicated pool in the interim if that speeds testing, but Private VPC is the target.

Available times for a technical call this week: Wed 10–12 PT, Thu 14–16 PT.

Thanks,
Lena
Lena Ortiz
VP Product, Acme Corporation
(lena@acmecorp.com)

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: private VPC eligibility & network questions

Thanks Lena — great, that helps a lot. Looping in our network lead Karthik Iyer and Monica from Customer Success to set up the technical sync and capture artifacts.

Short answers / what we can provide right away:
- PrivateLink: fully supported. We can publish a VPC Endpoint Service in our account and your team can create an Interface Endpoint in yours. This approach avoids peering and satisfies the "no peering" constraint.
- Static egress IPs: for PrivateLink, egress behavior depends on whether your interface endpoints are used for control plane or data plane traffic — we typically route inference traffic over the PrivateLink connection so you should not need public egress for inference. If outbound calls from our side to external third parties are required, we can route via a set of NAT IPs from a Dedicated egress pool if you need fixed egress IPs.
- KMS / keys: we support customer-managed KMS; our Private VPC flow can be configured to integrate with your KMS for model encryption at rest.
- mTLS: supported on dedicated endpoints; we can also provide TLS with cert rotation if mTLS is not required for your initial rollout.

To prepare for the technical call, please share:
- AWS account IDs and destination VPC ID(s)
- A high-level network diagram (attachable PDF or diagram link)
- Any external endpoints that must be allowlisted (we will map these to egress behaviors)

Karthik / Monica — can you propose two 30-min slots this week (Wed 10–12 PT, Thu 14–16 PT were acceptable to them) and confirm which artifacts we want them to prepare? I'm happy to join the technical call.

Best,
Dylan

Subject: Internal: Acme VPC technical prep checklist

Internal note (not sent to Acme):
Dylan — thanks for looping me in. Below is the checklist I'll bring to the technical sync. I'll attach a filled template and our recommended CIDR/eip ranges.

Pre-call artifacts to prepare (attach to HubSpot ticket):
- Redwood: service name, list of ports/protocols we require (typically TCP 443, TCP 22 for management if needed), required subnets for ENI placement.
- Acme: account IDs, VPC IDs, subnet IDs for interface endpoints, route table entries, and security group baseline.
- Egress mapping: list of external IPs/domains Acme needs to allowlist. If they require static egress, confirm whether they accept a set of NAT EIPs or need a vendor-specific solution.
- KMS flow: confirm Key ARN and whether cross-account grants are allowed.

Implementation options to present (pros/cons):
1) AWS PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint):
   - Pros: no peering, stays within AWS private network, compatible with their policy.
   - Cons: ENI quotas, interface endpoint scaling considerations, need to validate cross-account security groups.
2) VPC Peering / Transit Gateway:
   - Pros: fewer ENIs, simpler routing for multiple accounts behind TGW.
   - Cons: not compatible with their "no peering" policy today, more blast radius if misconfigured.
3) Hybrid approach: start with a small Dedicated pool for immediate testing (static egress), then cut over to PrivateLink once network config is validated.

I'll prepare: networking-checklist.xlsx (populated), vpc-architectural-diagram.png (recommended layout), and a short runbook for endpoint creation.

Planned next actions:
- Book Wed 11:00 PT technical sync with Acme (confirming with them now).
- Share populated checklist and diagram ahead of the call.

Karthik
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
